abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a severe neurological disorder characterized by axonal damage, myelin destruction, and motor and sensory dysfunction. This study employed mass spectrometry-based proteomic analysis to systematically identify differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) between sham-operated and SCI rats at post-injury time points (1, 3, 7, 14, and 28 days). 3-Hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 1 (HMG-CoA synthase 1, Hmgcs1) was identified as a key candidate protein. To investigate the role of Hmgcs1 in SCI repair, we utilized viral vector technology for functional studies both in vivo and in an in vitro co-culture system. Finally, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and quantitative reverse-transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) were integrated to elucidate Hmgcs1-mediated signaling pathways by validating downstream target gene expression. The results demonstrated that Hmgcs1 overexpression enhanced cholesterol synthesis in astrocytes post-injury, effectively promoted neuronal myelin repair, axonal regeneration, and improved motor functional recovery in rats. Notably, neuropilin-1 (Nrp1) expression exhibited Hmgcs1-dependent regulation.
